evidence.description: The shared instance is declared as nonisolated, while the class itself is annotated with @MainActor.

candidates.explanation: Declaring a nonisolated static property for a class annotated with @MainActor can lead to data races or unexpected behavior if the shared instance is accessed from different threads, as the class's properties and methods are intended to be isolated to the main actor.
candidates.title: Nonisolated shared instance of @MainActor class

evidence.description: A Task is created within the initialize method that performs asynchronous work without any mechanism to cancel or track the task.

candidates.explanation: Creating an unmanaged Task in a public initialization method can lead to race conditions or side effects occurring after the object is considered 'initialized' by the caller, and there is no way to cancel these tasks if the service is deallocated or re-initialized.
candidates.title: Unbounded Task creation in initialization

evidence.description: The UNUserNotificationCenter's delegate is set to self within a method that creates a local variable for the center.

candidates.explanation: Setting the delegate of UNUserNotificationCenter.current() to self inside a private helper method called during initialization might lead to unexpected behavior if the notification center is already being managed elsewhere or if the lifecycle of the service doesn't match the expected persistence of the notification center's delegate.
candidates.title: Potential Delegate Leak or Misconfiguration

evidence.description: The getBrazeConfiguration method uses a hardcoded default for the environment and a static property for the API key.

candidates.explanation: The configuration method relies on static defaults (BrazeService.apiKey and EcosiaEnvironment.current), which makes the service harder to test in isolation and couples it strongly to specific global environment states.
candidates.title: Tight Coupling to Environment Defaults

evidence.description: The braze delegate method checks for internal URLs and then interacts with an external browserDelegate.

candidates.explanation: The BrazeDelegate implementation mixes URL logic (host comparison), environment configuration, and UI navigation (browserDelegate), violating the Single Responsibility Principle.
candidates.title: Mixed Responsibility in Delegate Handling
